reason: E3 directly supports that grain boundaries promote internal oxidation and that ultrafine-grain microstructures can decelerate oxidation kinetics, but it shows refinement improves resistance, contradicting the premise that high grain boundary density accelerates degradation. E2 shows oxide exfoliation and matrix segmentation in a 3D-printed HEA but does not link this to grain boundary diffusion. E1 and E4 provide general oxidation mechanisms and alloying effects without addressing grain boundary density or spallation-driven failure. Thus, the key premises are either contradicted or unsupported
premises: Grain boundaries act as fast diffusion paths for oxygen or reactive species in HEAs
High grain boundary density accelerates formation of mixed Al-, Cr-, Ti-oxide scales
Nonuniform oxide growth creates internal stresses and decohesion at grain boundaries
Spallation of the oxide scale leads to catastrophic failure
Grain coarsening via annealing reduces grain boundary density and improves oxidation resistance
